Fresh official primary reads clarify why body normalization alone is insufficient. A binding anywhere in a function affects all its name references; global declarations can also override builtin lookup. Thus an erased new declaration can change meaning even if normalized statements match. [Pinned CPython execution model](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/2abcf904b8dac8c999d2b3aac76681abb333798a/Doc/reference/executionmodel.rst).

Python3.12 represents function type parameters separately from arguments, return annotations and body. [Pinned AST documentation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/2abcf904b8dac8c999d2b3aac76681abb333798a/Doc/library/ast.rst#L1754-L1769). Those parameters are available in the function body, so a matching body can resolve a formerly global symbol differently. [PEP695 scope specification](https://peps.python.org/pep-0695/#type-parameter-scopes).
